title: Agentic Safety Eval: Tool-Misuse Benchmark for Single-Agent Systems
original_idea: Design 100 scenarios where a user or injected content attempts to get a tool-using agent to perform harmful actions (delete files, exfiltrate data, execute malicious code). Evaluate two open-source agent frameworks and score refusal and detection rates.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Tool misuse is a top OWASP agentic risk. A lightweight benchmark directly addresses a documented safety gap.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing 100 tool-misuse scenarios and setting up agent frameworks with sandboxed tool access is substantial work. Requires understanding of agentic architectures. Hard for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 100 scenarios, 2 frameworks, multiple tool types. Benchmark design from scratch in 30 hours is very ambitious.

novelty.reasoning: ToolEmu (2024) provides 36 high-stakes tools and 144 test cases for identifying risky behaviors of LLM agents using tools. OpenAgentSafety (arXiv:2507.06134, 2025) is a comprehensive framework evaluating agent behavior across eight critical risk categories with real tools (browser, code execution, file system, bash terminal). InjecAgent (arXiv:2403.02691, 2024) provides 1,054 test cases covering 17 user tools and 62 attacker tools. The OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (Dec 2025) includes tool misuse (ASI02) as a key risk. The proposed 100-scenario benchmark is smaller and less comprehensive than existing work.
